Four colleagues X, Y, Z, W have ages in arithmetic progression with common difference 4 years, youngest to oldest. The sum of their ages is 100 years. What is Z's age?
questions.why: 4X + 24 = 100, so X = 19; ages 19, 23, 27, 31. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: agnoscrenia = poisonous spider; delanocrenia = poisonous snake; agnosdeery = brown spider. Which word could mean "black widow spider"?
questions.why: agnos = spider and comes first; the new word must start with agnos and use no known word. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: If 18 June 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 12 December 2025?
questions.why: 177 days later; 177 mod 7 = 2, so count 2 days on from Wednesday. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The average age of 15 students increased by 2 years when two students aged 14 and 18 were replaced by two new students. If one new student is 12 years older than the other, find the age of the younger new student.
questions.why: Total rises by 30, so new pair = 32 + 30 = 62. x + x + 12 = 62 gives 25. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Father, mother and son's ages sum to 70; the father is 6 times the son. When their total is 140, the father will be twice the son. How old is the mother?
questions.why: Total doubles after t = 70/3 years; 6S + t = 2(S + t) gives S = 35/6, F = 35, M = 70 − 35 − 35/6 ≈ 29 y 2 m. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: In a group of 80 people, 37 like tea, 37 like coffee and 27 like neither. How many like only tea?
questions.why: Both = 37 + 37 − (80 − 27) = 21; only tea = 37 − 21 = 16. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In how many different ways can the letters of the word REMEDY be arranged?
questions.why: 6 letters with repeats: 6! ÷ 2! = 360. GPSC-style practice item.
